questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=2,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{12(x-1)}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{12(x-1)}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{12{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{12}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{12}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{12}{x}+\frac{6}{{x}^{2}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =6-{2}^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{8}-\frac{1}{4},\, & 2\le x\le 6, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{2}^{6}x\cdot (\frac{x}{8}-\frac{1}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{x}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8})|}_{2}^{6} \\  & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{2}\cdot (\frac{x}{8}-\frac{1}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{4}}{32}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{12})|}_{2}^{6} \\  & =\frac{68}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{68}{3}-{(\frac{14}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{20(x-1)}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20x-20}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{20}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{20}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{4}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{20(x-1)}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20x-20}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{20}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{10}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{20}{3{x}^{3}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{10}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{10}{3}-{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{9}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈0.6931,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x+4}{24}, & -4<x<2 \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & 2\le x<4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x+4}{24}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{24}{\int }_{-4}^{2}({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{24}(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3}){|}_{-4}^{2}+x{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{11}{18}+\frac{8}{9}+2 \\  & =3.5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈3.5-(0.6931)^{2} \\  & ≈3.02.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=3,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{9}, & 0<x<3, \\ \frac{1}{9}(6-x), & 3\le x<6, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{6}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{6}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{6}{x}^{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{9}(6-x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{6}(\frac{1}{9}(6{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{36}|}_{0}^{3}+{\frac{1}{9}(2{x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})|}_{3}^{6} \\  & =\frac{21}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{21}{2}-(3)^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈1.238\,10,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{2{x}^{2}}{7}, & 1\le x<2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2{x}^{2}}{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{2{x}^{4}}{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{2{x}^{5}}{35}|}_{1}^{2} \\  & ≈1.882\,54\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈1.882\,54-(1.238\,10)^{2} \\  & ≈0.35\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=1,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1-x, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{10(x-1)}{{x}^{6}},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot (1-x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{10(x-1)}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{10x-10}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}){|}_{0}^{1}+(-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{10}{3{x}^{3}}){|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{1}{12}+0+5-\frac{10}{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}-{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot (\frac{x}{2}-\frac{3}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{12}|}_{0}^{2}+{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{4})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & ≈4.041\,67\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈4.041\,67-(1.791\,67)^{2} \\  & ≈0.83\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
The **variance** of a continuous random variable is the expected squared difference between the variable and its expected value.

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the variance is defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[(X-\text{E}[X])^{2}] \\  & ={\int }_{S}(x-\text{E}[X])^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

 

In practice, though, it's easier to use the following formula:

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2
$$

 

For example, consider the continuous random variable $X$ with the following probability density function:

$$
f(x) = \dfrac{x}{4}, \quad 1 < x < 3
$$

First, we compute $\textrm E[X]{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x\cdot \frac{x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{12}|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{13}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\textrm E[X^2]{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5-{(\frac{13}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$
